articles.title: Which coaches are on the hot seat heading into the NFL season? Aaron Glenn of the Jets leads the list
articles.summary: A handful of coaches enter this season under pressure.
articles.body:
The NFL had an offseason in which there was a record-tying 10 head coaching changes.

Next offseason might not see that many changes, but there will be some. NFL teams have become increasingly impatient and quick to change head coaches. There's even a notion that Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur, who has won 65.4% of his games and has just one losing season out of seven, could be on the hot seat if the Packers don't do well enough this season. Whether that comes to pass, it shows how tough of a profession it can be.

Here are the coaches on the hottest seats heading into the season:

Glenn was a candidate to be one and done after a very disheartening 3-14 season. Glenn stayed, but he replaced 12 of the 22 assistants from last year's staff. That type of turnover is a clear indication that the head coach needs to show improvement the following season. If the Jets are as uncompetitive as they were in Glenn's first season, it seems likely that a change would be made. And the Jets have plenty of roster holes heading into the season.

Bowles was in trouble after the Buccaneers went from 6-2 to losing seven of eight games and coming up short in the NFC South, which didn't have a single team over .500. The Buccaneers have arguably the most talented roster in the division, and if they can't win the division this season then there would be conversations over whether Bowles is the right coach for Tampa Bay going forward. He has a 35-33 record over four seasons as the Buccaneers' head coach.

The Bengals have missed the playoffs three straight seasons in Joe Burrow's prime. Injuries to Burrow contributed to two of those disappointing seasons, but at some point the Bengals need more urgency with Burrow still in his prime. Taylor is 52-63-1 in seven seasons as Bengals head coach. While patience paid off with a trip to the Super Bowl at the end of the 2021 season, the Bengals are 24-27 the past three seasons and would have to take a long look at everything if they miss the playoffs again.

It's rare in this era for coaches to miss the playoffs four times to start their tenure and still keep their job. Steichen has gone 0-for-3 in getting Indianapolis to the postseason, though quarterback issues including Daniel Jones' injury last season have been a valid excuse. The Colts were playing very well last season until Jones' torn Achilles ended his season. No matter the excuses, Steichen is one game under .500 as head coach and might need to make the playoffs to eliminate any discussion about his future in Indianapolis.

A year ago, it would have been shocking to see Quinn on this list. The Commanders were coming off a magical season that led to the NFC championship game. But last season was a huge step back, including Quinn admitting to a mistake having Jayden Daniels on the field in a blowout and seeing him dislocate his elbow. Then Quinn changed both coordinators in the offseason. There's usually only one move to make after that if the team doesn't improve. If the Commanders have soured on Quinn, they might quickly make a move to maximize Daniels being on his rookie contract.

articles.title: "Not being able to get up...": Patrick Mahomes’ heartbreaking words about his children make his remarkable Chiefs comeback even more meaningful
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has spent months racing against a recovery timeline that once seemed likely to keep him sidelined into the regular season. Now, the Ka.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has spent months racing against a recovery timeline that once seemed likely to keep him sidelined into the regular season. Now, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback appears poised for a stunning Week 1 return. But behind the intense rehabilitation was a motivation far more personal than football. His children gave Mahomes a reason to push through the hardest days and helped shape one of the most meaningful parts of his comeback.Patrick Mahomes turned his recovery into a personal raceMahomes suffered ACL and MCL injuries in December, putting his 2026 season in doubt. A typical recovery timeline suggested that the three-time MVP might not be ready until late September at the earliest.Instead, Mahomes attacked the rehabilitation process with the same competitive edge that has defined his NFL career.One of his earliest goals had little to do with throwing a football. His youngest daughter, Golden, was just 11 months old when Mahomes suffered the injury and was nearing the stage where she would take her first steps.Mahomes decided he wanted to walk before she did.That small personal target became an unexpected source of motivation during a demanding recovery. Working closely with athletic trainer Julie Frymyer, Mahomes managed to reach the milestone before his daughter and continued building from there.His progress has now put him in position to potentially start against the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football. Chiefs coach Andy Reid has not officially announced him as the Week 1 starter, but Denver is preparing as though Mahomes will be under center.Broncos coach Sean Payton has already made his expectations clear.“I’m going to probably say the same for Bo [Nix], you’ve seen enough things where he’s going to be 100%, and we’re preparing for him at his best,” Payton told reporters.“We know how talented he is, and I’m sure he’s attacked the rehab the way Bo has with completely different injuries. That’s kind of our approach to it.”For Mahomes, though, the biggest proof of progress came during training camp.“Being able to go out there, day after day, and have the grind of a camp, that can even be harder than the [regular] season, it’s been awesome for me to be able to do that,” Mahomes told reporters after not participating in the preseason.“It’s exciting. I didn’t know if I was going to have to take days off, but my body has responded the right way. Honestly, the more we practice, the better I feel.”Patrick Mahomes found his biggest motivation with his kidsThe physical work was only one part of the challenge. Mahomes has previously explained that the mental side of rehabilitation became particularly difficult when his injury stopped him from being an active father.“Honestly, the toughest part was at the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around,” Mahomes answered. “I know it sounds crazy, but being a dad and being active, I always want to be around my kids and playing and stuff like that. That was tough.”That changed once Mahomes could move around with his children again.“But once I was able to do that, it kinda motivated me to keep getting better and better. So, when Bronze has a T-ball game, or Sterling is playing soccer, I can be out there with them. I always knew I was going to get back to [training camp]. Just because of my mindset and the people around me. Once I was able to do that, it mentally helped me get through this process.”Mahomes now enters Week 1 with the possibility of turning an injury that threatened his season into another remarkable chapter of his career. The road back was built in the training room, but some of his strongest motivation came from simply being able to be there for his family again.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How fading intimacy and marriage concerns slowly changed Alix Earle’s relationship with Braxton Berrios
articles.summary: NFL News: Alix Earle did not announce the end of her relationship with Braxton Berrios with a statement. She drove a moving van to his Miami home, packed her th.
articles.body: Alix Earle did not announce the end of her relationship with Braxton Berrios with a statement. She drove a moving van to his Miami home, packed her things, and let the cameras roll. Her new Netflix series, *Earle Meets World*, opens with exactly that scene, and what follows across eight episodes is the most honest account yet of why her three-year relationship with the NFL wide receiver ultimately fell apart. Marriage pressure, fading intimacy, and a post-breakup encounter that left her stunned are all part of the story she now feels ready to tell.Why did Alix Earle and Braxton Berrios actually break up?The version of events the public received in December 2025 was brief. Sources said at the time that the majority of their relationship was long-distance and that they had mutually agreed on the split. That was accurate enough, but it left out a lot.On the show, Earle describes Berrios as her first real love, someone she once pictured growing old with. "Braxton and I were together for three years. He was the first actual, real love that I've ever experienced. I always said I could see us being old in rocking chairs together like, that's who I would want to be there with," she said.But the vision of that future also carried weight she was not ready to carry. "The thought, though, of Braxton ready for marriage in the near future really stressed me out. I'm only 25, and I'm not ready for that yet," she added.Alongside the marriage concerns, Earle acknowledged that intimacy between them had been quietly eroding. "It started to dwindle away a little bit," she said. Two people at different points in their lives, separated for stretches by NFL schedules and competing careers, and the closeness that once held things together was no longer enough. That, more than any single moment, appears to be what wore the relationship down.What happened between Alix Earle and Braxton Berrios after the breakup?Even after they split, the story had more to give. In the third episode of *Earle Meets World*, Earle recounts a night out where she ran into Berrios and tried to be honest with him about how difficult things had been. "He was mocking me, saying, 'I told you not to break up with me. Ha, ha, ha.' I was like, 'Wait, what?'" she told her sister and a friend. "He was laughing in my face. Like, 'I told you not to do this. I told you this was a mistake.'"She gave more context. "I had enough drinks to have the courage to go up to and say hi to Braxton," she said. "I must've said something along the lines of, 'This is really hard seeing you.' And I was trying to just be honest with him and I feel like that was not reciprocated."The season reportedly ends with Earle reaching out to Berrios to ask whether reconciliation was possible, which left fans unsettled and curious about where things now stand.What is going on between Alix Earle and Tom Brady?In the months after the Berrios split, Earle's name kept appearing alongside another one: Tom Brady. The two were spotted together around New Year's Eve in St. Barths, and further sightings during Super Bowl weekend added fuel to months of speculation.The Netflix series addressed it directly, without really addressing it at all. During a rehearsal session with her *Dancing with the Stars* partner Val Chmerkovskiy, his wife Jenna Johnson pressed Earle on the Brady rumors. "I don't know what's going on," Earle said. "I'm having fun." When pushed on whether anything was confirmed, she simply replied, "No, I'm just having fun," before adding: "I know, a lot has changed since last time."Brady, for his part, has not mentioned Earle by name, though he has said previously that he does not have much time for romance right now. Whatever is or was happening between them, neither has chosen to define it publicly and Earle seems comfortable keeping it that way.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I'm a Hell of a Football Player,' C.J. Stroud Addresses Criticism and New Rumors on Texans Contract
articles.summary: Ahead of what could be an important year for him financially, Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud struck a confident tone.
articles.body:
Ahead of what could be an important year for him financially, Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud struck a confident tone.

"I play this game because God has chosen me to go through these things and to have this talent," he told ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime . "Got some guys around me that want to protect and want to run the ball. So I think that'll help, and I'm a hell of a football player."

Stroud hit the ground running as a rookie. He averaged an NFL-best 273.9 passing yards and had 23 touchdowns to five interceptions en route to being a Pro Bowler.

Late NFL Additions Who Could Influence 2026 Super Bowl Hopes

Since then, the 24-year-old has regressed. In 31 starts across 2024 and 2025, he threw for 6,768 yards, 39 touchdowns and 20 interceptions. That averaged out to 218.3 yards per contest.

The fact the Texans haven't extended Stroud past the 2027 season — he has a $25.9 million club option next year — speaks for itself.

With so much on the line, he's trying to avoid the outside noise.

"People are quick to use Twitter," Stroud said. "I focus on me. I can't control [social media], so why would I care? Of course I'm human. I learned if some people had the opportunity to be me, they would. But a lot of people have opinions and don't have opportunities.

"So the more opinions people have, the more opportunity that I have to prove who I am. They love to critique. That's part of life. I play in an entertainment sport, so they're critical of a lot of people. I have the opportunity to go play. No one can stop that."

The signal-caller added he's "proud of myself for how I've handled these past couple months" and spun his past struggles on the field in a positive light. They've provided him with an opportunity to improve.

Every NFL player wants long-term financial security, and Stroud would presumably prefer to have a lucrative extension in hand. Bien-Aime reported he and the Texans are at least "content" with where things stand.

Stroud has the full support of the locker room as well. Wide receiver Nico Collins told Bien-Aime the quarterback is "built for everything."

"We believe in him, we love him," Collins said. "This is the best position he can be in right now. I feel like he is about to go out and show the whole world what he's made of, and I can't wait. We got his back 100%, all the way."

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported on Sept. 2 the Texans are "prepared to put Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club." The player appears to be unmoved given the parties haven't struck an agreement yet.

That's a little risky when $50 million would represent fair value for Stroud. The Dallas Cowboys' Dak Prescott and Kansas City Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes are the only QBs earning $60 million or more.

Should Stroud have a monster campaign, he could plausibly hit that valuation. In the event that fails to happen, his future earnings could take a massive hit.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Teams Eyeing 2027 Draft Picks in Anticipation of Hyped Class
articles.summary: Teams around the NFL are placing a premium on 2027 draft capital, according to ESPN's Field Yates.
articles.body:
Teams around the NFL are placing a premium on 2027 draft capital, according to ESPN's Field Yates.

At the 19:03 mark in the newest episode of the First Draft podcast, Yates noted general managers are content to sell off some 2028 picks rather than ones next year.

"I've had people around the league tell me that's also not a coincidence," he said. "Teams want as much 2027 skin in the game as they can get because there are premier players. And when you have a lot of quarterbacks that are going to go, there are teams that don't need a quarterback. … If you're the Las Vegas Raiders, you want 10 of these QBs to ball out. You want every single one of them to look like the next John Elway because that means good players get pushed down to a team like you."

To further underline his point, Yates pointed to the Cincinnati Bengals' trade for Dexter Lawrence. Giving up the No. 10 overall pick for the three-time Pro Bowler, who had a down year in 2025, reflected how the 2026 draft class wasn't considered exceptional.

The assessment was especially true at quarterback, with Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson the only ones picked in the first two rounds.

That contrasts quite a bit with 2027. In Bleacher Report's newest mock draft , four quarterbacks were projected to go in the top eight: Miami's Darian Mensah, Texas' Arch Manning, Oregon's Dante Moore and Notre Dame's CJ Carr.

ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. also threw USC's Jayden Maiava into the Day 1 conversation. The longtime draft expert suggested Ohio State's Julian Sayin, Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss are among the others who could eventually earn a first-round grade.

Pivoting away from quarterback, you have Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, who looked NFL-ready from the moment he debuted with the Buckeyes. He earned a 9.8 overall grade from the B/R NFL Scouting Department.

Notre Dame's Leonard Moore is the best cornerback in college football. Texas' Colin Simmons and South Carolina's Dylan Stewart could make a big impact off the edge at the next level.

Obviously, nobody knows right now how the 2027 draft class will pan out. It's easy to see why NFL talent evaluators are excited based on what evidence they do have.

articles.title: Top Week 1 Waiver Wire Pickups from 2026 NFL Preseason
articles.summary: With the arrival of the 2026 NFL season, it's tempting to give all of you fantasy football managers a hearty "Congrats!" on a draft season well done.
articles.body:
With the arrival of the 2026 NFL season, it's tempting to give all of you fantasy football managers a hearty "Congrats!" on a draft season well done.

Unfortunately, your work is far from finished. In fact, it sort of just started.

Because all you've done so far is assemble your first roster. Now, you have to properly handle it by nailing your start-or-sit lineup decisions and perpetually working the waiver wire for potential upgrades. Speaking of, there are already waiver-wire targets (rostered in fewer than 50 percent of leagues, per FantasyPros ), so let's get them on your radar asap.

Tyler Allgeier, RB, Arizona Cardinals (21% Rostered)

Even when Arizona was operating at full-strength, it was giving goal-line work to Allgeier. Which should surprise no one. The 5'10", 225-pounder is such a short-yardage asset that he managed to 15 rushing scores over the past three seasons despite sharing a backfield with Bijan Robinson.

After moving to Arizona, Allgeier's competition for carries are now rookie Jeremiyah Love, who is working his way back from a high ankle sprain, and veteran James Conner, who landed on injured reserve with a foot ailment.

Given Allgeier's handcuff appeal, he probably should've been more rostered already, especially once the Cardinals tipped their goal-line plans for him.

But with question marks about Love's availability, Allgeier feels like a must-roster in all but the shallowest leagues.

Jordan Love, QB, Green Bay Packers (28% Rostered)

Ever since Love erupted for 4,159 passing yards and 32 touchdowns in 2023, the Packers have dialed back his usage to the point of robbing him of standard league-relevance. They have stressed the ground game like a team with a shaky quarterback, even though he has completed nearly 65 percent of his passes with 48 touchdowns against 17 interceptions the past two seasons.

If this is the year in which Green Bay reconfigures its offensive approach, Love might be in line for the best campaign of his career.

Less congestion in the receiving room could lead to more clarity of that hierarchy and perhaps a better connection with the top playmakers. Josh Jacobs' placement on the commissioner's exempt list could force the Packers to lean into their passing game. Love also draws one of the most favorable schedules for fantasy quarterbacks.

This all feels like stars-aligning fortune coming together for Love. Add him now before a potential Week 1 effort skyrockets his rostership.

Tyjae Spears, RB, Tennessee Titans (24% Rostered)

Spears has long tantalized with sleeper talent. He's also three years into his NFL career and has yet to produce 500 rushing yards or six-plus scores in a season.

For some, that will be a sign he may never awaken. For others, it's a reminder that development doesn't always happen on our preferred timeline, making patience an absolute must.

Especially when patience may no longer be needed.

Spears saw more preseason snaps with the Titans starters than Tony Pollard did, which could the early indication of a changing of the guard. With Tennessee still trudging through a rebuild, one can only assume it would prefer the 25-year-old Spears to wrestle control of this backfield away from the 29-year-old Pollard (who isn't signed beyond this season).

articles.title: “More than 1000 concussions”: Aaron Rodgers’ predecessor Brett Favre battles Parkinson’s disease as latest video leaves fans concerned
articles.summary: NFL News: Every NFL analyst says that they see Brett Favre in Aaron Rodgers. For years, Brett Favre was the NFL’s ultimate symbol of gridiron toughness.The Gree.
articles.body: Every NFL analyst says that they see Brett Favre in Aaron Rodgers. For years, Brett Favre was the NFL’s ultimate symbol of gridiron toughness.The Green Bay Packers legendary quarterback played through immense pain, absorbed brutal hits, and kept getting back up. Now, the Hall of Fame quarterback is facing perhaps the toughest battle of his life - Parkinson’s disease.Favre was diagnosed in January 2024 and publicly revealed his condition later that year. In his latest health updates, he acknowledged that the disease has progressed “a little faster” than he had hoped for it to. But he has made one thing crystal clear: he has not given up hope and he won’t ever.“I’m just praying for a cure for me and millions out there who have the same disease,” Favre told TMZ in Jan. 2026. “I’m early. Even though it’s been three years, it’s still early in this disease, so I’m holding out hope something can at least stop the progression, if not cure it.”Aaron Rodgers’ predecessor Brett Favre’s Parkinson’s battle follows years of football hitsThe heartbreaking part of Brett Favre’s story is how closely it is related to the game that made him an NFL legend.Favre believes he could have suffered more than 1,000 concussions during his football career of 20 seasons, 321 consecutive starts including 297 regular season games. That figure is his own estimate, not a medically verified count.He has explained that only a few of his concussions were formally diagnosed, while other hits left him with symptoms as seeing stars, flash bulbs, or experiencing ringing in his ears.At the moment, Favre has spoken about dealing with rigidity and severe stiffness, particularly on his right side, along with occasional shaking. He has also continued pursuing treatment options and clinical trials. Notably, he said he biked more than 6,200 miles in 2025.It is a deafening contrast to the pictures fans remember of him: Favre sprinting onto the gridiron, taking another hit and throwing another pass.The football career is over. The physical battle is still with him.Aaron Rodgers and Brett Favre’s Green Bay Packers connection hits differently nowBrett Favre’s health battle undoubtedly brings Aaron Rodgers into the conversation.The two ace quarterbacks are permanently linked in the Green Bay Packers history. Aaron Rodgers spent three seasons behind Brett Favre in Green Bay before ultimately becoming his successor.Both became Super Bowl champions, both earned reputations as fearless gunslingers and both became defining figures of different Packers eras: Favre in 1996-97 and Rodgers in 2010-11.Their similarities extend beyond statistics, achievements, and championships. Both quarterbacks built their careers around confidence, aggressiveness, high-risk and high-reward passing styles, toughness, and a willingness to withstand the punishment that comes with playing behind center [read: under center].Favre has also continued to discuss Rodgers, including recently weighing in on whether his former protege has enough left to play another season.“Aaron still can play,” Favre said on his podcast in Feb. 2026. “It’s a matter of whether he wants to play and will someone take a chance on him. I think if he really wants to play, someone will take a chance on him. Maybe Pittsburgh. The relationship with he and [Mike] McCarthy certainly is intriguing.”Two quarterbacks. Two generations. One unforgettable Packers connection.Brett Favre’s latest fight is far bigger than footballPerhaps the most inspiring part of Favre’s post-football story is what he has chosen to do with his Parkinson’s experience.In 2026, he said he wanted to connect with former Packers teammate Ahman Green after Green publicly revealed his own Parkinson’s diagnosis. Favre understands the fear and uncertainty that can come with the disease, and his willingness to support another former teammate gives his story a special dimension.“The amount of head/neurological issues among the former players is staggering,” Favre told TMZ in July 2026.The 56-year-old MVP recorded a video over the weekend for the Green Bay Packers’ Mexican fans ahead of the 2026 NFL season. This video has fans concerned about his health, especially after the Parkinson’s disease diagnosis.For decades, fans watched Favre fight defenders on the gridiron. articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. Injury Update Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Tua Named Falcons' QB1
articles.summary: While the Atlanta Falcons officially named Tua Tagovailoa their Week 1 starting quarterback over Michael Penix Jr., it sounds like Penix remains on track in his recovery from a torn ACL.
articles.body:
While the Atlanta Falcons officially named Tua Tagovailoa their Week 1 starting quarterback over Michael Penix Jr., it sounds like Penix remains on track in his recovery from a torn ACL.

According to Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated , Penix "has been fully cleared," but the third-year signal-caller is "still working his way back from the injury, so Atlanta's being careful here."

"This isn't Tua Tagovailoa beating him out," Breer stated. "More so, it's about Penix's readiness."

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski later told reporters that Penix will be inactive on Sunday.

Penix was forced to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering a partially torn ACL in November. He didn't play in any of Atlanta's three preseason games, and he wasn't cleared to participate in 11-on-11 team drills until the final week of training camp. Still, the 26-year-old told reporters prior to the preseason finale last month that he feels healthy enough to start in Week 1.

This marks the sixth straight year that Atlanta will open the season with a new starting quarterback.

The Falcons signed Tagovailoa to a one-year deal after he was released by the Miami Dolphins, who took on a whopping $99.2 million in dead cap to get him off their roster. He started two of Atlanta's preseason games, going 3-of-5 for 22 yards against the Denver Broncos and 7-of-8 for 95 yards against the Dolphins. He fumbled a snap in both outings, and ESPN's Marc Raimondi noted that the six-year veteran "was unable to push the ball downfield with regularity, which was also an issue in training camp practices."

For now, it will be Tagovailoa running the show for the Falcons as he tries to prove he can be a dependable starting quarterback, but Penix should eventually get the chance to reclaim his spot as Atlanta's QB1.

articles.title: New Travis Hunter Rumors Update Jaguars' Outlook for 2-Way Star Entering 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars continue to see Travis Hunter as a two-way player, but he may prove to have one clear area of expertise.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars continue to see Travis Hunter as a two-way player, but he may prove to have one clear area of expertise.

The MMQB's Albert Breer reported Monday the Jags "believe [Hunter] can become a shutdown corner," and the player "has since turned his focus to defense."

Fans didn't get a full picture as to whether the 2024 Heisman Trophy can effectively play offense and defense in the NFL. His rookie season ended after seven games, and his usage at cornerback was a little sporadic .

Jacksonville isn't abandoning the experiment just yet.

"We'll definitely have a package on offense to be able to get him some opportunities," coach Liam Coen said in August on The Rich Eisen Show (7:45 mark). "There's been a steady increase in his defensive work just by nature of where we're at on defense and continuing to try to create consistency. ... There's been a lot of detail and time-on-task this offseason. He'll absolutely have a plan on offense."

Coen's remarks do, however, reinforce the idea the Jaguars see Hunter as a cornerback first and a receiver second. That generally aligns with how evaluators viewed him heading into the 2025 NFL draft.

The Bleacher Report NFL Scouting Department assessed him as a corner and compared him to eight-time Pro Bowler Patrick Peterson.

There's a pragmatic aspect at play beyond wanting to avoid putting too much on Hunter's plate.

Parker Washington took a big step forward in his third year. Brian Thomas Jr. should rebound after going backwards a bit in 2025. And Jakobi Meyers is a very good No. 3 option through the air. Jacksonville's receiving corps is in a solid place.

The same can't be said of the secondary. Greg Newsome II, who started 11 games following a midseason trade from the Cleveland Browns, left as a free agent and created a void at cornerback. The pass defense as a whole needs to improve after ranking 21st in yards allowed (218.1 per game).

The Jaguars could use an elite defender out wide, and that's exactly what Hunter may prove to be.

Coen can still deploy him as a pass-catcher in the right situations. Fans shouldn't be surprised, though, if there's a clear split in where he's lining up on a weekly basis.

articles.title: Latest NFL Rumors on Baker Mayfield Contract Talks Ahead of Bucs' Opener vs. Burrow, Bengals
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield declared that he won't engage in contract discussions before the end of the 2026 season, and it sounds like he's sticking to that stance.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield declared that he won't engage in contract discussions before the end of the 2026 season, and it sounds like he's sticking to that stance.

Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated reported that "there haven't been any substantive negotiations since the start of camp" between Mayfield and the Bucs, who are set to open the year against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.

Mayfield ended contract negotiations with Tampa Bay before the start of training camp, declaring that he felt "disrespected" by what the team initially offered. Still, Bucs general manager Jason Licht expressed confidence that the team will be able to retain him by the end of the year.

"I'm very optimistic about it," Licht said during the WFLA broadcast of the Bucs' third preseason game at the Jacksonville Jaguars, per ESPN's Jenna Laine . "He wants to play. He wants to prove to us that he is the franchise quarterback that we said that he was. So, we'll just have to see how it plays out. I'll never close the door on anything in the short term, but right now, he's focused on football."

Breer noted that he feels there's still a chance for Mayfield and the Bucs to re-engage in contract talks before Sunday's season opener, pointing out that "the two sides weren't that far apart earlier in the summer." He also highlighted Tampa Bay's "willingness to get a market deal done closer to the season," as evidenced by the team's deals with Tristan Wirfs, Zyon McCollum, Luke Goedeke and Vita Vea over the last two years.

Mayfield hasn't been known to change his mind often, so it remains to be seen if he will budge before he takes the field against the Bengals on Sunday.

articles.title: Why Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running isn’t as popular as Patrick Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes have become two of the most prominent faces of the Kansas City Chiefs, but their charitable foundations have develope.
articles.body: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes have become two of the most prominent faces of the Kansas City Chiefs, but their charitable foundations have developed very distinguished standards of public visibility.While Kelce’s 87 & Running continues to make a substantial impact, Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies Foundation appears to have attained mightier mainstream commendation. The difference has less to do with the value of their work and more with branding, reach, and public exposure.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running has a more focused missionTravis Kelce founded Eighty-Seven & Running in 2015 with a sincere mission shaped by his childhood experiences in Cleveland Heights, Ohio.He grew up in a community transcending normal economic and cultural boundaries, where rich and poor, black and white, and different religious affiliations merged into one big melting pot.Because of this, Kelce witnessed that some of his close friends did not have the same family structure he was blessed with and were not able to enjoy the same experiences as he did.Some of his role models did not come back to the community to support their hometown. He wanted to do that. He came back and founded the 87 & Running organization for his community.The 87 & Running Foundation focuses on empowering disadvantaged and underserved youth to gain access to opportunities, enrichment, and advancement in education, business, athletics, STEM, and the arts.Its work includes programs such as the Operation Breakthrough Ignition Lab in Kansas City, which provides teenagers aged 14-18 from under-resourced neighborhoods with cutting-edge equipment, a safe environment, essential resources, committed mentorship, and opportunities to explore STEM potential and unleash their entrepreneurship.That genre-focused approach could be one reason 87 & Running can sometimes receive less general-public recognition. Its identity is tightly tied to youth development and opportunity rather than a broad collection of highly visible celebrity events.Why 15 and the Mahomies has greater brand recognitionPatrick Mahomes’ Foundation was founded four years after 87 & Running’s inception, in 2019. It has a straightforward branding advantage: the number “15” is inseparable from Patrick Mahomes himself.The phrase “15 and the Mahomies” instantly connects his Kansas City Chiefs jersey number with his widespread supporters, creating an unforgettable identity that naturally extends beyond football.The quarterback may have taken the idea of “15” from “87 & Running.” “87” is Travis Kelce’s jersey number. But we all know that an NFL quarterback is the soul of the gridiron; he is powerfully placed in a stronger position than a hybrid pass catcher like a tight end.Anyhow, Mahomes’ Foundation is wholeheartedly dedicated to improving children’s lives by supporting initiatives involving education, health, wellness, underserved communities, and other charitable causes.It has also built highly visible partnerships, including a national collaboration with Boys & Girls Clubs of America.Other charitable partners include Children’s Mercy, Make A Wish, Youth Volunteer Corps, Kids Feeding Kids, Black College Football Hall of Fame, Special Olympics, Variety, the children’s charity of Kansas City, among others.The Foundation’s annual gala, ever since its inception, has further strengthened its impactful profile. The sixth annual gala, held in October 2025, was promoted as a major Kansas City philanthropic event. The event raised $1.5 million for 27 Kansas City charities from more than 900 supporters.87 & Running still has a powerful legacyIt would be extremely unfair to take lower visibility for lower impact. 87 & Running has been operating longer than the 15 and the Mahomies foundation. Kelce’s organization actively continues to invest in meaningful programs designed to give youth access to unattainable opportunities they might otherwise lack.The only supposed difference is ultimately one of public branding. Mahomes’ Foundation benefits from an instantly distinct name, extremely visible partnerships, and a charitable identity closely connected to his Chiefs jersey No. 15.Kelce’s 87 & Running has a similarly purposeful mission, but its substantial work often speaks for itself rather than taking the center stage or monopolizing the limelight.For Kelce, that could be the takeaway point. His Foundation’s success isn’t measured by how loudly its name is recognized, but by how many youths it truly impacts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Matt Suhey Dies at 68, NFL Legend Won Super Bowl with Bears in 1985
articles.summary: Former Chicago Bears fullback Matt Suhey died Sunday at the age of 68.
articles.body:
Former Chicago Bears fullback Matt Suhey died Sunday at the age of 68.

Suhey spent his entire 10-year career in the Windy City. Across 148 appearances, he ran for 2,946 yards and 20 touchdowns. He was on the famed 1985 squad that won a Super Bowl title and had an 11-yard touchdown run in the 46-10 blowout of the New England Patriots.

Clearing running lanes for Walter Payton was Suhey's most frequent duty on the field. The Athletic's Dan Pompei detailed in 2024 how the pair eventually forged a strong connection off the field.

Payton and Suhey drifted apart as their playing careers ended. The former retired after the 1987 season and the latter was out of the league two years later.

As Payton went through his cancer battle resulting in his death in 1999, the one-time teammates reconnected. According to Pompei, Suhey would drive Payton to appointments or on random errands, and they would spend time together at Payton's home.

"Walter was a loner," Connie Payton said of her late husband. "There weren't a lot of people he would hang out with. He was strange like that. But I knew Matt was special to him and near to his heart because he allowed him to be in his space."

Prior to the Bears selecting him in the second round of the 1980 NFL draft, Suhey played four years at Penn State. He had 3,146 yards from scrimmage and 28 touchdowns in 42 games.

articles.title: Tua Tagovailoa gets a stunning second chance as Falcons make their Week 1 quarterback decision
articles.summary: NFL News: Tua Tagovailoa has another NFL starting job, but this one comes with far less certainty than the one he left behind in Miami. The Atlanta Falcons name.
articles.body: Tua Tagovailoa has another NFL starting job, but this one comes with far less certainty than the one he left behind in Miami. The Atlanta Falcons named Tagovailoa their Week 1 quarterback on Monday, ending their long competition with Michael Penix Jr. The decision puts the veteran in line to start against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, six months after the Dolphins released him following a difficult 2025 season. For Tagovailoa, this is more than a fresh uniform. It is a chance to show Atlanta that his career still has another productive chapter left.Why did the Falcons choose Tua Tagovailoa over Michael Penix Jr.?The most important detail behind Atlanta's decision is not that Tua Tagovailoa clearly outplayed Michael Penix Jr. It is that he was the quarterback who was ready to play.Penix missed the preseason while recovering from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season. He was eventually cleared for full-team work, but that came late in training camp. Tagovailoa, meanwhile, handled most of the first-team reps and started both the first and final preseason games. That gave him a clear advantage when the Falcons had to decide who could operate the offense immediately.That distinction matters because Tagovailoa did not exactly force Atlanta's hand with an outstanding summer. His preseason numbers were solid, but there were mistakes along the way. Against Miami, his former team, he completed 7 of 8 passes for 95 yards and opened the game with a touchdown drive, but he also lost a fumble. Atlanta still saw enough from the veteran to trust his preparation.The Falcons also have a reason to value what Tagovailoa can provide right now. His game is built around timing and getting the ball out quickly, which can help an offense stay on schedule. Atlanta has playmakers such as Bijan Robinson and Drake London, so the coaching staff does not necessarily need Tagovailoa to turn every possession into a deep-passing showcase.Can Tua Tagovailoa turn this into a long-term comeback?That is the more interesting question.Tua Tagovailoa's opportunity in Atlanta comes after a sharp decline in Miami. He threw 15 interceptions in 2025 and was benched late in the season. The Dolphins then released him in March, despite having given him a four-year, $212.4 million extension in 2024.Now he has a one-year deal and a starting role that could change quickly.The Falcons did not hand Tagovailoa a long-term commitment. Penix remains on the roster and is viewed as the younger quarterback with a potential future in Atlanta. The team also kept four quarterbacks, an unusual level of insurance that reflects how unsettled the position remains.That makes Sunday especially important. Tagovailoa does not need to prove everything in one afternoon, but he does need to give Atlanta reasons to keep believing. His last game in Pittsburgh was also his final start for Miami, a loss that preceded his benching. Returning to the same city with a different team gives this comeback an unusual twist.For now, Tagovailoa has what he wanted: the ball, the first-team offense and another chance. What happens next will determine whether this is simply a Week 1 decision or the beginning of something bigger.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Who was Matt Suhey? Chicago Bears fullback and 1985 Super Bowl champion died at the age of 68
articles.summary: NFL News: Matt Suhey, the Chicago Bears fullback who helped the team win Super Bowl XX, has died at 68. Suhey died Sunday, Sept. 6, NBC Chicago reported. He spe.
articles.body: Matt Suhey, the Chicago Bears fullback who helped the team win Super Bowl XX, has died at 68. Suhey died Sunday, Sept. 6, NBC Chicago reported. He spent all 10 of his NFL seasons with Chicago after the Bears selected him in the second round of the 1980 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He became a key part of the 1985 championship team and was also known as Walter Payton’s longtime lead blocker and close friend.Who was Matt Suhey, the Chicago Bears fullback?Matt Suhey was born on July 26, 1958, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and came from a football family. His father, Paul Suhey Sr., played football at Penn State, while his older brother, Paul Suhey, played in the NFL for the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl XIII.Suhey followed his family’s football path to Penn State, where he played running back. The Chicago Bears selected him 39th overall in the second round of the 1980 NFL Draft.Suhey became an important part of Chicago’s backfield, especially as a lead blocker for Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton. He helped create running room for Payton while also contributing as a runner and receiver.Suhey and Payton became close friends and formed an important partnership during the Bears’ successful 1980s run. Suhey spent his entire 10-year NFL career with Chicago and retired in 1989.How did Matt Suhey’s Chicago Bears career become part of NFL history?Suhey played 148 regular-season games for the Bears, starting 100 of them. He finished his NFL career with 2,946 rushing yards and 20 rushing touchdowns on 828 carries. He also caught 260 passes for 2,113 yards and five receiving touchdowns, according to the Chicago Bears.His biggest individual moment came on the sport’s biggest stage.In Super Bowl XX in January 1986, Suhey scored Chicago’s first touchdown with an 11-yard run against the New England Patriots. The Bears went on to win 46-10, giving the franchise its first Super Bowl title.That play gave Suhey a lasting place in the story of the 1985 Bears. He was part of a team remembered for its dominant defense, strong running game and larger-than-life personalities, but his role was often about making things easier for the stars around him.Suhey never missed a game during his 10-season Bears career. He retired from the NFL in 1989 after spending his entire playing career with Chicago.Even after leaving football, Suhey stayed connected to the Bears and his former teammates. The team later included him among its top 100 players, ranking him No. 70.His death adds another loss to the group that helped create one of the most remembered teams in Bears history. For Chicago fans, Suhey’s story is tied not only to the numbers he produced, but also to the work he did for Payton and the role he played in the Bears’ first Super Bowl championship.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Despite naming Deshaun Watson as the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback and Shedeur Sanders as his backup, head coach Todd Monken left the door open for rookie signal-caller Taylen Green to see some action in Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Monken told reporters on Monday that Sanders and Green are splitting practice reps as the scout-team QB and said that Green could have a package of plays installed for him on Sunday.

"Could be. There could be a package where we have him," Monken said.

Monken was also asked if having three quarterbacks active on game day would be too many.

"If we can afford it, it would be nice to have five or six quarterbacks up," Monken said before admitting, "but three is a lot."

A sixth-round pick in this year's draft, Green made Cleveland's 53-man roster after second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel was placed on injured reserve due to a back injury. articles.title: Niners DC Raheem Morris 'misses' his entire 50th birthday while traveling to Australia
articles.summary: Raheem Morris missed all of Sept. 3, somehow.
articles.body:
On Sept. 3, San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris turned 50. Unfortunately for him, he wasn't able to celebrate … because he missed the entire day.

Due to the 49ers' travel schedule, Morris kinda skipped that date entirely. With the 49ers playing in Australia in Week 1, the team decided to fly down a week early to properly adjust to the time change .

Because of that, the team left at night on Sept. 2. But — thanks to the time change — when they landed, it was Sept. 4 in Australia. Morris "missed" his entire birthday.

If you're confused about how that works, and how days and time are … a little different when traveling from the United States to Australia, well, you wouldn't be the only one.

When asked about preparing for the game, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan gave the most confusing answer when trying to break down how the team is preparing each day.

"We're a little confused with, when I look at my clock, and it says the time and then I try to see my family's time and it says the time, but it says yesterday, I don't even get how that's possible. So I feel like I'm in the future. "And then also when we play on our Friday, which I think is a Thursday in the U.S., we're such creatures of habit, so I call today Tuesday. No, wait, sorry. I call today Wednesday, which is the first day we put in a game plan. But I think it's Monday. However, though, it's Sunday in the present. So, like, I'm going to mess that up all week if you guys ask me. "Today is just our first day of the game plan, which is a Wednesday. We'll put in some on a Thursday. Friday's the final part of the game plan. Saturday, we walk through and we play on Sunday, which is a Friday in Australia and a Thursday in the U.S. So, don't ever make me do that again."

"We're a little confused with, when I look at my clock, and it says the time and then I try to see my family's time and it says the time, but it says yesterday, I don't even get how that's possible. So I feel like I'm in the future.

"And then also when we play on our Friday, which I think is a Thursday in the U.S., we're such creatures of habit, so I call today Tuesday. No, wait, sorry. I call today Wednesday, which is the first day we put in a game plan. But I think it's Monday. However, though, it's Sunday in the present. So, like, I'm going to mess that up all week if you guys ask me.

"Today is just our first day of the game plan, which is a Wednesday. We'll put in some on a Thursday. Friday's the final part of the game plan. Saturday, we walk through and we play on Sunday, which is a Friday in Australia and a Thursday in the U.S. So, don't ever make me do that again."

In the end, we're guessing (hoping?) Morris got to have some type of celebration on the team's flight to Australia. While he may not have technically experienced Sept. 3, it did happen. He is 50 now. And hopefully the team acknowledged as much, even if the day was a bit of a blur for the coach.

articles.title: Cowboys LG Tyler Smith to undergo thumb surgery, expected to miss 4-6 weeks
articles.summary: Smith has dealt with a ligament issue in his thumb for some time, according to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith will undergo thumb surgery and be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday.

As a result, the three-time Pro Bowler will be placed on injured reserve. The injury is to a ligament in Smith's thumb and had been bothering the fifth-year veteran for some time, according to Schottenheimer.

articles.title: Darius Slayton Released by Giants, Updated NFL Salary Cap, Depth Chart and Top Landing Spots for WR
articles.summary: The New York Giants are moving on from one of their veteran wide receivers.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are moving on from one of their veteran wide receivers.

The team announced on Monday that it has released Darius Slayton after seven years with the team. Slayton was the longest-tenured member of the Giants.

The 29-year-old was entering the second year of a three-year, $36 million deal and had a $15.91 cap hit for the upcoming season. New York was $953,427 over the cap before releasing Slayton, per Spotrac .

With Slayton on his way out of New York, a handful of teams in need of wide receiver depth might try to pick him up. The New Orleans Saints, Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans jump out as potential candidates.

The Giants drafted Slayton in the fifth round in 2019, and he's managed to put together a strong career, amassing 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns over the past seven years.

Last season, he had 538 yards and a touchdown on 37 receptions. While it wasn't a bad year by any means, it was his lowest production since 2021, and heading into the offseason, it was possible that Slayton wouldn't be on the team to start the 2026 campaign.

Still, Slayton believed he could have been a key piece in the Giants' offense under new head coach John Harbaugh.

"Just another playmaker," Slayton told reporters about his fit on the team. "I feel like we have a bunch in the room, a lot of really talented guys that we've added to the roster. I see myself as one of those guys and whatever capacity that I can be."

While the Giants perhaps needed some depth at wide receiver with Calvin Austin out for the year, they decided it was time to part ways with Slayton, and he'll look to end up somewhere else.

The Saints are in desperate need of some wide receiver depth heading into the season, but they can't afford much given their salary cap position. Slayton would be an affordable option since the Giants are paying him guaranteed money for the 2026 campaign.

The Eagles likewise could use some depth after Johnny Wilson suffered a season-ending injury, so they could pick up Slayton after their divisional rival decided to release him.

The Titans are still hoping to get Cam Ward comfortable in his second season, and picking up a veteran like Slayton could further his development.

articles.title: Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed deserves more credit, Mike Elko says
articles.summary: Marcel Reed is already moving up Texas A&M's record book. Mike Elko thinks the quarterback's best work is still being overlooked
articles.body:
COLLEGE STATION - Texas A&M coach Mike Elko wants people to have a greater appreciation for starting quarterback Marcel Reed.

"I wish people would spend more time studying him and watching him and seeing how good he really is," Elko said during his Monday press conference.

"As he continues to move up the all-time passing record at Texas A&M , and he starts to move past some quarterbacks who are very successful quarterbacks here and viewed as very successful quarterbacks here, I wish people would start to appreciate who he is, what he does and how successful he's been for us as a starter."

Following Saturday's 50-0 season opening victory over Missouri State, Reed sits in seventh in Texas A&M history passing yards and passing touchdowns and fifth in total touchdowns responsible for. Only Heisman Trophy winner Johnny Manziel ranks ahead of Reed in total offense per game and passing efficiency rating. Reed is also the only quarterback to lead the Aggies to the College Football Playoff.

When asked for one aspect he wished people would appreciate more of Reed's game, Elko said "all of it."

"How good of a quarterback he is. How much he helps us win football games. How successful he's been. How many yards he throws for. How many yards he runs for," Elko said.

One person who had plenty of praise for Reed was Arizona State head coach Kenny Dillingham.

Dillingham said during his Monday press conference in Arizona that people don't give Reed enough credit for his "unbelievable touch" in the intermediate passing game and on the deep ball. He also highlighted the difficulty in sacking Reed.

"Then you can tell he's gotten way more comfortable in true dropback passing," Dillingham said.

Reed started his senior season completing 21 of 30 passes for 233 yards and two scores, along with a couple of key scrambles for positive yardage, in the blowout victory over the Bears.

Saturday's win, played in front of a record crowd (107,782) for a Texas A&M season opener, moved Reed to 16-6 as a starting quarterback for the Aggies.

"I thought there was a lot of progress in him going through progressions and reads," Elko said. "I thought there was a lot of progress in the timing and how the ball came out of his hands. Obviously completing a very high percentage of his passes was good. That was a big emphasis for him and for us."

Expectations were high for a more-consistent and less-turnover-prone Reed entering the season. He made the watch lists for the Maxwell Award, the Walter Camp Award and the Davey O'Brien Award but didn't make ESPN's list of the top 100 players in college football or any of the preseason All-SEC teams.

One game against an overmatched opponent won't change many minds. But Reed has at least 11 more games to turn more people to Elko's point of view.

"I still have stuff I need to improve on," Reed said Saturday night after the win. "But I think for the first game, for the most part, I did what I was supposed to do. I'll go look on Sunday, like I said, and just make the adjustments I need to for going forward."

articles.title: Monday Musings: Mali-Mensah mania; next man up for Miami
articles.summary: Happy Monday, errrrrrrbody. And for the first time since January, HAPPY VICTORY MONDAY! The Miami Hurricanes triumphed over the Stanford Cardinal 45-6, and a...
articles.body:
Happy Monday, errrrrrrbody. And for the first time since January, HAPPY VICTORY MONDAY!

The Miami Hurricanes triumphed over the Stanford Cardinal 45-6, and as such, the 2026 run to No. 6 got off on the right foot.

Lots to talk about, so let's get down to brass tacks.

1) The Miami Hurricanes have a…complicated Heisman Trophy problem. And that's a great thing.

Malachi Toney went absolutely bonkers, setting the program records with 234 receiving yards. He is completely unguardable right now and the best overall player in college football regardless of position. Yes, put that in ink. His routes like crisp and sharp, and it even looks like he accelerates out of the break perhaps a step faster than last year.

And now he has a first-round talent throwing him the ball downfield in Darian Mensah. Mensah looked damned incredible. 27/30 for 401 yards and 5 touchdowns.

But for me it came down to two throws that really set the tone for his game, and it showed an NFL-level touch and anticipation that you just can't teach.

I mean, that throw to Arroyo was put in a spot that a lot of NFL quarterbacks aren't going to put it. And the back shoulder location to Upshaw on the touchdown was perfect and unguardable. You just don't see that type of placement from many college QBs.

So now, I think the Hurricanes have two legit and strong Heisman Trophy contenders on their roster. And the interesting thing is that they will both be supplementing each other's resumes every single week. Toney is a 100+ yard weekly receiving ATM machine. Take that straight to the bank. Mensah looks every bit as advertised for a $6 million quarterback, and between Toney, Cooper Barkate, Daylyn Upshaw/Joshua Moore and others, it's going to be an explosive and potentially record-setting year.

The only thing I hope is that, by both drawing Heisman Trophy consideration, they both don't lose enough votes for one or the other to get clipped by December. But hell, what a situation to be in for Miami.

2) The injury Gods weren't too kind to Miami.

Starting CB OJ Frederique is out with a "pretty significant injury" that will keep him out for "quite a while", per Mario Cristobal. That's a tough break. Frederique went down with an upper body injury on Stanford's first drive of the game, and he never returned. Damari Brown filled in, and I thought he acquitted himself quite well (even if PFF didn't think so, as I noted in my piece from earlier today).

Will we see Corey Hetherman find a way to get JJ Dunnigan on the field more as a result somehow? They love him, and he looks like a special, special player in the making. I'm curious to see how this rotation looks moving forward.

3) Looking down the road a bit, but Miami's game against Clemson might have created an interesting opportunity for the Hurricanes.

I thought Miami's second toughest game of the year was going to be Clemson on the road, and it still won't be a total cake walk per se. It's at Clemson, and they have athletes, and anything can happen as such. But MY. GOD. What an embarrassment on Saturday night in Baton Rouge. That team stinks.

Someone pointed out on Twitter a reminder of how Dabo and his Tigers annihilated Miami and helped deliver the final nail in the coffin of Al Golden in 2015. Yeah, the game where they never went to the locker room. Perhaps a cruel bit of irony could be delivered by the 2026 Hurricanes, as Dabo's seat is certainly more than warm after 7-6 last year and a horrid start this year.

articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys lose $96 million All-Pro to surgery before season opener vs. New York Giants. The post Dallas Cowboys Lose $96 Million All-Pro for Season Open...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys won't have the NFL's elite interior offensive lineman against the New York Giants for their primetime season opener on Sunday.

"Cowboys All-Pro LG Tyler Smith is scheduled to undergo thumb surgery Tuesday and is expected to be sidelined 4-6 weeks, per Dallas HC Brian Schottenheimer," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Monday.

Smith's surgery is scheduled for Tuesday.

"Tyler Smith is set to have surgery on his left thumb and will be placed on injured reserve, which will cost him the first four games of the season," ESPN's Todd Archer wrote on X. "Smith has been bothered by the injury for some time and was trying to avoid surgery. TJ Bass will start at left guard."

"Cowboys All-Pro LG Tyler Smith is set to have thumb surgery, coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on Monday. "He's out at least four weeks and headed to Injured Reserve. TJ Bass will fill in for Smith."

Tyler Smith Bona Fide Superstar in Dallas

The Cowboys have a genuine superstar leading their offensive line with Smith, who was voted the NFL's No. 1 interior offensive lineman by league executives, coaches, and scouts on Sunday, moving up 1 spot from last year's rankings.

At just 25 years old and with a 4-year, $96 million contract signed in September 2025, that bodes pretty well for the future.

"Rare combination of size, athleticism, strength and finish," an anonymous AFC executive told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "He's like prime Jason Peters playing guard."

Peters was a 9-time Pro Bowl and 6-time NFL All-Pro offensive tackle who helped lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a Super Bowl win following the 2017 season and even spent a season with the Cowboys in 2022.

"Smith is the league's highest-paid guard, and for good reason," Fowler wrote. "The 2022 first-round pick has worked his way from offensive tackle prospect to elite guard with three consecutive Pro Bowls. His win rates of 72.1% in the running game and 95.2% in the passing game are quality but not elite numbers. But to watch him is to value him."

Second Offseason Surgery for Tyler Smith

Smith, 6-foot-5 and 328 pounds, decided to participate in the Pro Bowl Games following the season, and before he underwent knee surgery .

"All-Pro OL Tyler Smith had cleanup surgery on his right knee after the Pro Bowl but will be 100% ready for the offseason program, per sources," ESPN's Todd Archer wrote on his X account on February 24. "He dealt with the issue during the season, dressing but not playing against the Jets ."

Smith was a 1st-round pick (No. 24 overall) in the 2022 NFL draft out of Tulsa. In 4 seasons, Smith is a 3-time Pro Bowl selection and earned NFL All-Pro honors in 2023.

articles.title: Ex-Georgia DB JaCorey Thomas Commits to WVU – What You Need To Know
articles.summary: Today we received news that JaCorey Thomas committed to WVU. He has received a temporary restraining order against the NCAA in order to get a 5th year of eli...
articles.body:
Today we received news that JaCorey Thomas committed to WVU. He has received a temporary restraining order against the NCAA in order to get a 5th year of eligibility. I break down everything you need to know about this confusing, but much needed defensive back commit.

JaCorey Thomas played 4 seasons with the Georgia Bulldogs. He started every game for the Georgia in 2025 and recorded 45 tackles and a sack. He played his high school football in Orlando, FL and was listed as a 4 star recruit by Rivals.

JaCorey Thomas declared for the 2026 NFL Draft after his senior year at Georgia. He went undrafted, but received an invitation to participate in the Carolina Panthers rookie minicamp which took place on May 8 – 9 2026. He did not receive a roster spot after the rookie minicamp and has been an unsigned free agent since then. When a court ruled that 2022 college signees would qualify for a fifth year of eligibility, he declared that he would be entering the college transfer portal.

What's the Difference Between This and What Lane Kiffin is Doing?

Let me start this out by saying that JaCorey Thomas did declare for the NFL Draft, did not withdraw his name, and spent time in an NFL Rookie minicamp. Full stop. With that said, there are differences in how he has spent his time since last season compared to Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who are returning from the NFL to LSU for Lane Kiffin. Both Wright and Harris were signed as undrafted free agents, took part in a full NFL training camp, and were even on preseason rosters for NFL teams before being waived. This means that both Wright and Harris would have had NFL contracts, whereas JaCorey Thomas would have only received a per diem and travel expenses paid without a contract for attending a Rookie minicamp. JaCorey's situation is actually more similar to that of Tommy Castellanos, the quarterback that just committed to Texas Tech after participating in the Miami Dolphins Rookie minicamp.

Did you watch the Coastal Carolina game? We will take all the help we can get in the secondary and I would have to think that Zac Alley would love to have a former starter at Georgia in his toolbox. The question is will we risk it given that the Big 12 has put out statements expressly forbidding teams from signing former NFL players? Well Texas Tech hasn't let that stop them. Tommy Castellanos dressed and actually saw playing time for them in their week 1 game. With the court ruling last week, technically teams should be allowed to sign these players regardless of what the conferences are saying. But even Lane Kiffin didn't dress the 2 players in question for the Clemson game. When asked why he basically said that he has to look out for the long term health of LSU. To me it sounded like he didn't want to make the SEC mad. It seems pretty clear the rule that was UNANIMOUSLY adopted by the Big 12 member schools would forbid JaCorey Thomas from playing based on this verbage: "Member schools cannot roster any athlete who has joined a professional sports league roster, signed a professional contract, or failed to withdraw on time from a professional draft." The part about failing to withdraw on time from a professional draft would be the sticking point with JaCorey Thomas unless I'm missing something. So the way I understand it is that with the most recent court ruling he could legally play for WVU, but at this point it seems to go against the rules that the Big 12 and other conferences have passed in recent weeks. Sigh…

What do you think about this? Do you want to see him play this year?

articles.title: NFL 2026 Bets: MVP Props For Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, Jahmyr Gibbs
articles.summary: Explore a trio of top NFL MVP bets to consider ahead of the start of the 2026 season, including past winners Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is now just days away, affording bettors only a short period of time to capitalize on some potentially profitable preseason futures bets.

Sportsbooks offer a host of NFL futures, with many of those focused on end-of-season awards. One very popular betting market of this type involves the AP Regular-Season MVP Award, and as customary, this year's leaderboard is replete with notable names.

Ahead of Wednesday's Patriots-Seahawks kickoff that will officially cut the ribbon on the 2026 regular season, here's a trio of MVP contenders to consider:

Allen is a perennial MVP contender thanks to his elite dual-threat ability, and nothing has changed on that front heading into the 2026 season.

In fact, an argument could be made Allen is ideally set up for a second regular-season MVP award in the coming campaign. That belief stems from both a significant offseason acquisition at receiver in the form of DJ Moore, and a change at head coach to Joe Brady, who's previously served as Allen's quarterbacks coach and offensive coordinator .

Allen's passing volume has been down over the last two seasons , and with James Cook's breakout 1,621-yard campaign on the ground a year ago, the prolific signal-caller could be under 500 attempts again during the coming regular season. However, Cook is also a capable receiver and Allen has priceless continuity in the form of several very familiar targets to work with, not to mention his considerable comfort level with Brady.

Allen also averaged a career-high 8.0 yards per attempt last season, and his new No. 1 receiver Moore does have the ability to make plenty of plays downfield and produce after the catch. Finally, it's worth noting Allen has double-digit rushing TDs in three straight seasons, and he put up the second most of his career (14) in 2025.

Jackson is another supremely talented, versatile quarterback who typically finds himself near the top of the MVP futures market leaderboard.

This year, there's a bit of value to be had in the form of four-digit odds for a player who's already secured two MVP awards. Jackson comes into 2026 having fully recorded from the hamstring and back injuries that he now says significantly limited his mobility last season, and he's once again surrounded by a collection of familiar and capable skill-position weapons.

Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews once again are set to comprise Jackson's top three targets , a trio of pass catchers the talented signal-caller is highly familiar with. Jackson has also shown a welcome trend toward more aggressive downfield passing in recent seasons, averaging at least 8.0 yards per attempt in three consecutive campaigns.

Jackson rushed a career-low 67 times last season (next fewest-112), so the aforementioned injuries do appear to have legitimately had an impact. Assuming Lamar can enjoy a much less physically demanding 2026 and gets back over the 700-yard rushing mark he'd previously made the norm throughout his career, he should very much be in play for this award by year's end.

If looking for an intriguing non-QB longshot that has a realistic shot at pulling an upset for this award, Gibbs is certainly worthy of consideration.

The fourth-year back is the recent beneficiary of a massive three-year extension worth up to $75.75 million, a figure that underscores the value the Lions place in the explosive back. The breadth of the investment also speaks to how much usage awaits Gibbs in 2026, especially now that former backfield mate David Montgomery is in Houston.

Gibbs already averaged 18.8 touches per game in 2025 , and that was with Montgomery vulturing 10.7 percent contest as the complementary option. In turn, Gibbs' primary backup to open the 2026 season, Sione Vaki, has only seven career carries over his first two seasons, while No. 3 option Jacob Saylors does have plenty of UFL experience but was used almost exclusively on special teams in his 2025 NFL debut campaign.

Isiah Pacheco's (back) eventual return from injured reserve will ostensibly present some competition for touches, but Gibbs is naturally the clear-cut top option in the ground game and unlikely to cede too much opportunity. Given he also plays half his games on the fast track of Ford Field and is an elite receiver (career-best 77-616-5 line in 2025) in addition to a game-breaking runner, Gibbs is a legitimate high risk/high reward proposition in this market.
